text.tspan: Next, we will put the entire process together using technology. From this point on, we will use
STATBELT and its option to type in the summarized data to find the sample proportion, test statistic,
and P-Value. However, if you only have access to Desmos, or a free probability distribution calculator,
you can still find the test statistic first, then get the P-Value using the probability calculator. Don’t
forget to double the area of the tail if you follow that path and conduct a two-tailed test.
